institutionName: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As an English BA, I mainly focussed on study destinations where English was spoken to truly test and advance my English proficiency. Furthermore, I had always dreamt of studying and experiencing the American culture and their University unity that would place me in a completely different environment than the one I was used at KU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It should be taken into consideration, that choosing a study destination such as the US will truly test your abilities to stand on your own in a culture completely alienated from what you know.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, I mostly contacted staff at KU or my exchange university if I was confused or needed assistance.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A fair amount. A lot of e-mails was sent out from the exchange university's internations student coordinator that helped remind us about important dates and things we needed to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The host university had a lot of different options ranging from having  your own bed, to your own room, to your own apartment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The meal plan was also one I paid for. The exchange university had a variety of meal plan options; full meal plan, part-time meal plan, 100 swipes to access dining hall etc. Plus they had multiple dining halls and a broad variety of foods.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I truly enjoyed living on Campus as for me it was a big part of the exchange experience and immersing myself into the environment. I lived in a large apartment with both Americans and other exchange students which was perfect.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Again, we were a lot of internation/exchange students as it was in the fall, therefore, I had a lot of friends who like me also needed assistance and seeked help to process their registration. Furthermore, the international student coordination was also a great help in this process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at my host university was smooth and efficient. From the moment I arrived, the staff were welcoming and well-organized, guiding me through every step. The online portal was user-friendly, and all necessary information was provided in clear, timely emails. I felt supported and confident as I completed the registration, and the orientation sessions offered helpful insights into university life.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international student coordinator was my personal choice as he always answered right away and was available through phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. One just had to be careful about the choices they made for choosing classes as their was a deadline where change no longer could happen.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Stay calm. It will all work out, I promise. There are only a few things that are so important that if you miss them they can mess with your stay but 9 times out of 10 missing a deadline, misunderstandings and things you did not know will not disturb your exchange. Talk with other exchange students and better to e-mail an extra time than not at all.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a 24 y/o undergraduate it was difficult at times being with 18-20 year olds but I think its both an age and culture barrier, but with no doubt part of the experience. But the programs provided where very good and there was a broad range of choices to pick from.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels are different no doubt. Furthermore, some classes may feel easier but others harder. Prepare for mid-terms, because once they start they do not end. It will be a steady stream of exams, so remember to take time to prepare.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was definitely the most different. In the US, students are expected to show up and participate where at UCPH they provide flexibility and choice, furthermore, the choice to self-study. Be prepared to spend a great amount of time both in and out of class as they also expect that you answer the quizzes and read up on texts etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Topics in Literature and Film: American Horror in Fiction and Film.
Intro to Fiction Writing.
Topics in English: Introduction to Linguistics.
Global Arts/Humanities: Global Connections in English Studies.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I have no specific courses to advocate for but I do however, recommend to try a few that are different from your degree as I did. It is good learning and a fun experience.

questions.answer: Trips, adventures, and stuff related to this.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and food was more expensive than expected but outside of this it felt reasonably priced.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a great deal of clubs and sports available. I used both the gym and pilates classes every week for free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Cultural Activities:
- Theatre and performing arts.
- Art exhibits.
- Cultural celebrations like international festivals and heritage month events.

Athletic Activities:
- Club sports (soccer, tennis, etc.).
- Sports leagues (basketball, volleyball, flag football).
- NCAA Division I teams (Charlotte 49ers) with events and games which was one of the best parts!

Social Activities:
- Student organizations covering academics, hobbies, and social causes.
- Campus events like welcome week, concerts, movie nights, and mixers.
- Popp Martin Student Union did social events, trivia nights, and karaoke.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join Student Organizations, attend Campus Events, get involved in intramural or Club Sports, volunteer or participate in Community service, explore Local Culture and Events, and explore the outdoors around campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel! Go with friends to other states or cities. Plan ahead and make time as it goes by so fast! Explore your own city, visit museums, cafe's, and theme parks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Just be openminded then it will work out. I was prepared as I knew that I was going to live in a Southern state.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be prepared and opens for differences in culture and how they build connections. Americans for example are very open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The openess, as a Dane, could sometimes be difficult to tackle as we pride ourselves on personal space and not being rude, intrusive etc. whereas Americans do not have that concern at all.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Somehow also the Americans openess, it felt different and nice to meet so many people who were so friendly and talkative.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get Involved: Join clubs, sports, or events to connect with others and dive into campus life.
Explore the city: Take time to explore the city and nearby nature spots for a well-rounded experience.
Be Open-Minded: Adapt to cultural differences and embrace new experiences for personal growth.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic experience and growth. The culture differences. Traveling to places I wanted to see. The people !!!!!!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Homesickness without a doubt, as the only Dane there, with barely any Scandinavians it was a hard time when there were large groups of Germans, Italians and British who could understand each other and share where they came from. Be prepared, use your friends and family back home and make sure to educate, and share your languages and country with others. Make Denmark proud!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
